en: to be false; to be fake; to be fabricated

examples.en: What he said sounded false.
A fake smile shows right away.
I later found out that the rumor was untrue.
I apologized with a sincere heart.

examples.ko: 광고 속 이야기가 거짓된 것으로 밝혀졌어요.
examples.en: The story in the ad turned out to be false.

examples.ko: 거짓되고 겉만 번지르르한 말에 속지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't be fooled by fake and showy words.

explain: '거짓말이에요', '가짜예요'를 더 자주 써요. '거짓되다'는 사람의 마음, 말, 웃음이 진실하지 않다는 느낌으로 글이나 조금 무거운 대화에 나와요. 반대말은 '참되다', '진실하다'예요.

phrases.en: False words don't last long.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거짓된'은 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요. 진실하지 않은 말이나 마음에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form modifies a noun. It is used for words or feelings that are not sincere.

phrases.en: His apology doesn't seem insincere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진심이라는 뜻을 부정형으로 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft way to say something seems sincere, by negating the word.

phrases.en: That excuse sounds false.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 사람이 진실하지 않다고 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the listener feels that something is not sincere.

explain_en: In daily talk 거짓말이에요 or 가짜예요 are more common. 거짓되다 describes words, smiles, or feelings that are not sincere, mostly in writing or serious talk. Its opposites are 참되다 and 진실하다.

examples.en: This monitor is high resolution, so the text is sharp.
Please send me a high-resolution photo.
High-resolution video takes up a lot of storage.
The new phone's screen changed to high resolution.
If you print in high resolution, the picture is cleaner.

examples.ko: 고해상도 이미지는 파일이 무거워서 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: High-resolution images are heavy files, so they take a long time.

explain: '저해상도'와 짝이에요. 말로는 '화질이 좋다', '선명하다'도 많이 써요. 'HD', '4K'처럼 이름이나 숫자로 말하는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.example: 고해상도 화면으로 영화를 보니 정말 좋아요.
phrases.en: Watching movies on a high-resolution screen is really nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모니터, 휴대폰, TV 화면을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe monitors, phones, and TVs.

phrases.en: I'll take the photo in high resolution and send it to you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진이나 영상을 선명하게 찍는 방식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes taking photos or videos in a sharp, detailed quality.

phrases.en: This camera has good picture quality.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고해상도'보다 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual in everyday conversation than 고해상도.

explain_en: The paired word is '저해상도'. In speech people also say '화질이 좋다' or '선명하다'. Names or numbers such as 'HD' and '4K' are also commonly used.

examples.en: That actor's smiling eyes are really charming.
The baby smiled with its eyes when it saw me.
She greeted me with just a smile of her eyes.

examples.ko: 동생이 눈웃음을 지으면서 용돈을 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: My sibling flashed a sweet smile and asked for pocket money.
With a single smile from his eyes, the mood relaxed.
That person has a pretty eye-smile.

explain: 입보다 눈으로 살짝 웃는 웃음이에요. '눈웃음을 치다'는 호감을 보이거나 애교를 부릴 때 쓰고, 상황에 따라 약간 꾸민 느낌도 줄 수 있어요. 따뜻한 칭찬으로는 '눈웃음이 예쁘다'가 많아요.

phrases.en: The baby gave me a sweet smile with its eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호감을 보이거나 애교를 부릴 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for showing liking or being cute.

phrases.en: My older sister has a lovely eye-smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃는 눈이 보기 좋다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment on someone's smiling eyes.

phrases.en: He greeted me with a smile in his eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치다'보다 꾸민 느낌이 적고 자연스럽게 웃는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels less put-on than 치다, a more natural smile.

explain_en: It is a smile made more with the eyes than the mouth. '눈웃음을 치다' is used when showing affection or acting charming, and can sometimes sound a bit put-on. As a compliment, '눈웃음이 예쁘다' is common.

examples.ko: 그는 배짱이 두둑해서 발표 전에도 떨지 않아요.
examples.en: He has plenty of nerve, so he does not shake even before a presentation.

examples.ko: 배짱 좋게 사장님께 월급을 올려 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: With real nerve, I asked the boss to raise my pay.

examples.ko: 그런 말을 하다니 정말 배짱도 좋네요.
examples.en: You have some nerve to say something like that.
I have no guts and only a lot of worries.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 배짱으로 마지막 공을 던졌어요.
examples.en: The player threw the last ball with sheer nerve.

examples.ko: 배짱만 믿고 시험 준비를 안 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You should not rely only on guts and skip exam preparation.

explain: '용기'는 좋은 뜻으로 많이 쓰고, 배짱은 겁 없이 버티는 힘이에요. 상황에 따라 칭찬도 되고 '뻔뻔하다'는 흉도 돼요. '배짱이 두둑하다', '배짱 좋다', '배짱을 부리다'로 써요.

phrases.example: 값을 깎아 주지 않으면 안 사겠다고 배짱을 부렸어요.
phrases.en: I said I wouldn't buy it unless they lowered the price, and I held my ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁 없이 버티거나 고집을 부릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone holds firm without fear.

phrases.example: 저는 배짱이 없어서 노래를 못 불러요.
phrases.en: I have no nerve, so I can't sing in front of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁이 많고 용기가 부족하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone is timid and lacks nerve.

phrases.en: A person with guts has an advantage in interviews.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 꾸밀 때 쓰고 보통 좋게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person, usually in a positive way.

explain_en: 용기 is mostly a positive word, while 배짱 is the power to hold on without fear. Depending on the situation it can be praise or a complaint like 뻔뻔하다. It appears as 배짱이 두둑하다, 배짱 좋다, and 배짱을 부리다.

examples.en: Please stop with the pointless jokes.

examples.ko: 그의 대답이 시답잖아서 더 묻지 않았어요.
examples.en: His answer was so unconvincing that I didn't ask more.
I'm worried the present will look unimpressive.
To me, all of that talk is trivial.
That movie's plot was really lame.
He looked at me with a face that said I was not worth his time.

explain: '시답지 않다'를 줄인 말로, 마음에 차지 않거나 하찮고 별것 아니라는 느낌이에요. 보통 '시답잖은 농담/소리/일'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 말해요. 상대의 말을 낮춰 보는 느낌이 있어서 사람 앞에서는 조심하세요.

phrases.en: Stop talking nonsense and get to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하찮은 말을 낮춰 볼 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used to dismiss trivial talk.

phrases.example: 그 일은 시답지 않아서 신경 안 써요.
phrases.en: That matter is trivial, so I don't care about it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시답잖다'를 줄이지 않은 원래 형태로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The un-contracted original form of 시답잖다, with the same meaning.

phrases.en: He regarded my suggestion as worthless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것을 하찮게 본다는 뜻으로, '-게 여기다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to regard something as trivial, using -게 여기다.

explain_en: It is a contraction of '시답지 않다', carrying the feeling of unsatisfactory, trivial or not worth much. It usually comes before a noun, as in '시답잖은 농담/소리/일'. It sounds dismissive, so be careful using it about what someone says to their face.

examples.ko: 모든 일에는 좋은 면과 나쁜 면, 양면이 있어요.
examples.en: Everything has two sides, a good one and a bad one.

examples.ko: 이 종이는 양면에 인쇄할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can print on both sides of this paper.
I stuck the photo down with double-sided tape.

examples.ko: 문제를 한쪽만 보지 말고 양면을 살펴보세요.
examples.en: Don't look at only one side of a problem; look at both.
The internet has two sides, convenience and danger.

examples.ko: 양면 복사를 하면 종이를 아낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: Copying on both sides saves paper.

explain: 양면은 물건의 앞뒤, 또는 어떤 일의 좋은 점과 나쁜 점처럼 서로 다른 두 쪽을 함께 말할 때 써요. 물건에는 '양면 테이프', '양면 복사'처럼 붙여 쓰고, 생각을 말할 때는 '양면이 있다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I stuck the photo on with double-sided tape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞뒤 두 쪽이 끈끈한 테이프를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tape that is sticky on both sides.

phrases.en: I made double-sided copies to save paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이 앞뒤에 복사할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for copying on both sides of the paper.

phrases.example: 이 일에는 좋은 점과 나쁜 점, 양면이 있어요.
phrases.en: This matter has two sides, good and bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 좋은 점과 나쁜 점이 함께 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something has both good and bad sides.

explain_en: Yangmyeon refers to two different sides together, such as the front and back of an object or the good and bad of a situation. For objects it appears in 양면 테이프 and 양면 복사; for ideas, 양면이 있다 is common.

en: to be fastidious; to be particular; to be unusual

examples.ko: 빨간 코트를 입은 사람이 사람들 사이에서 유난히 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: The person in the red coat stood out unusually among the crowd.

examples.ko: 오늘따라 보름달이 유난히 크고 밝아서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The full moon was especially big and bright tonight, so I took a photo.
This winter feels especially long.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때부터 겁이 유난히 많았어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has been especially timid since childhood.

examples.ko: 그는 유난한 성격이라 같이 있으면 피곤해요.
examples.en: He has such a fussy personality that it is tiring to be with him.

examples.ko: 유난한 더위 때문에 에어컨을 하루 종일 켰어요.
examples.en: Because of the exceptional heat, I ran the air conditioner all day.

explain: 실제로는 '유난히'의 형태로 가장 많이 쓰이고, '유난히 크다/예쁘다'처럼 다른 것보다 눈에 띄게 다르다는 느낌을 줘요. '유난하다' 자체는 '유난한 날씨'처럼 쓸 수 있지만 '유난히'보다 드물어요. 사람에게 '유난이다/유난 떨다'라고 하면 지나치게 호들갑스럽다는 말이 돼요.

phrases.en: This winter is unusually cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유난하다'보다 '유난히'를 훨씬 자주 써요. 뒤에 형용사를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 유난히 is far more common than 유난하다; an adjective follows it.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 키가 커서 유난히 눈에 띄어요.
phrases.en: That person is tall, so they really stand out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 것보다 확 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something stands out much more than others.

phrases.example: 감기에 걸렸다고 왜 그렇게 유난을 떨어요?
phrases.en: Why are you making such a fuss just because you caught a cold?
phrases.nuance_ko: 별일 아닌데 지나치게 행동할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 조금 부정적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone overreacts to something minor; slightly negative.

explain_en: In practice it appears most often as '유난히', as in '유난히 크다/예쁘다', meaning noticeably different from the rest. The adjective itself, as in '유난한 날씨', is possible but rarer than '유난히'. Saying '유난이다/유난 떨다' about a person means they make a bigger fuss than necessary.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 유력 후보로 꼽히고 있어요.
examples.en: He is considered a leading candidate.
Many influential figures attended the event.
Our team is a leading contender to win.
The news said a prime suspect was caught.

examples.ko: 이번 달 안에 결정될 것이 유력해요.
examples.en: It looks likely to be decided within this month.

examples.ko: 유력 일간지가 이 소식을 먼저 보도했어요.
examples.en: A major daily newspaper reported this news first.

explain: 유력은 '유력 후보'처럼 명사 앞에서 가장 가능성이 높거나 힘이 있다는 뜻으로 많이 붙어요. 형용사 '유력하다'는 '우승이 유력하다'처럼 쓰고, 뉴스에서 특히 자주 나와요. '유력 후보', '유력 용의자'처럼 한 덩어리로 기억하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: That player is a leading candidate to win.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 가능성이 높은 후보를 가리키는 뉴스 속 대표적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical news phrase for the candidate with the best chance.

phrases.en: It's likely that our team will win.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사로 써서 어떤 일이 일어날 가능성이 높다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as an adjective to say something is highly likely.

phrases.en: The police found the prime suspect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건 뉴스에서 가장 의심받는 사람을 말할 때 한 덩어리로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a set phrase in crime news for the most suspected person.

explain_en: 유력 is most often attached before a noun to mark the most likely or most powerful one, as in '유력 후보'. The adjective '유력하다' is used as in '우승이 유력하다' (the win looks likely) and appears a lot in the news. It is easiest to remember as a chunk like '유력 후보' or '유력 용의자'.

examples.en: This place's kimchi stew is the best in the neighborhood.
In our class, Minsu is the best at running.
Health comes first, so don't overdo it.

examples.ko: 으뜸 상품으로 뽑힌 책이 정말 재미있어요.
examples.en: The book chosen as the top item is really fun.
I learned that manners are the top virtue.
That singer's song is counted as the best.

explain: 으뜸은 여럿 가운데 가장 뛰어나거나 가장 중요한 것을 말해요. '최고'와 비슷하지만 으뜸은 순서에서 맨 앞이라는 느낌이 있어서 '으뜸가는', '으뜸이다'처럼 써요. 말할 때보다 글이나 광고에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: This restaurant is the best eatery in the neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으뜸'이 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 말이 되어, 가장 뛰어난 것을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This turns 으뜸 into a modifier, used to introduce the very best of something.

phrases.example: 사람들은 이 노래를 올해 으뜸으로 꼽아요.
phrases.en: People pick this song as the best of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿 중에서 가장 좋은 것을 골라 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when choosing the best one out of many.

phrases.en: This place's kimchi stew is the best in the neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 으뜸과 비슷한 말인데, 최고는 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word to 으뜸, but 최고 is more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: 으뜸 means the most excellent or most important among many. It is close to 최고, but 으뜸 carries a feeling of being first in the order, and appears as 으뜸가는 or 으뜸이다. You see it more in writing and ads than in speech.

en: to be vulgar; to be low-quality

examples.ko: 그 농담은 너무 저급해서 웃을 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: That joke was so crude that I couldn't laugh.

examples.ko: 저급한 말투를 쓰는 사람과는 얘기하기 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't want to talk with people who use vulgar language.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 값이 싼 대신 품질이 저급해요.
examples.en: This product is cheap but the quality is poor.

examples.ko: 그 방송은 저급하다는 비판을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: That broadcast is being criticized as low-grade.
It's a funny movie whose humor isn't crude.

examples.ko: 일부러 저급하게 만든 광고라서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The ad was deliberately made to look cheap, so it got people talking.

explain: 수준이나 품질이 낮다는 평가를 강하게 할 때 써요. 물건의 품질보다는 말, 취향, 유머, 문화 같은 '수준'에 더 많이 쓰고, 사람에게 직접 말하면 아주 무례해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '고급스럽다'예요.

phrases.en: Please stop the vulgar jokes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수준이 낮은 말이나 유머를 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize low-quality talk or humor.

phrases.en: That ad looks kind of cheap.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉모습이나 인상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -아/어 보이다 it describes an impression.

phrases.example: 이 프로그램은 수준이 낮아서 안 봐요.
phrases.en: I don't watch this show because its quality is low.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저급하다'보다 덜 강하고 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less harsh and easier to use than 저급하다.

explain_en: It is a strong judgment that the level or quality of something is low. It is used more for the 'level' of language, taste, humor and culture than for the quality of objects, and saying it directly to a person is very rude. The opposite feeling is '고급스럽다'.

en: to be poor; to be coarse

examples.ko: 이 장난감은 너무 조잡해서 금방 부서졌어요.
examples.en: This toy was so shoddy that it broke right away.
The poster design looks a bit crude.

examples.ko: 조잡한 물건은 사지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to buy cheaply made goods.
The sentences in this translation are rough.

examples.ko: 가짜 상품은 마감이 조잡하게 되어 있어요.
examples.en: Fake goods are crudely finished.
The product was rated as poorly made, so I returned it.

explain: 물건, 솜씨, 글, 디자인이 정교하지 못하고 거칠다는 뜻이고, 싸구려 같다는 느낌이 있어요. '허술하다'는 빈틈이 있다는 느낌이고 '조잡하다'는 짜임이나 만듦새가 거칠다는 느낌이에요. 사람의 성격보다는 만든 것에 써요.

phrases.en: The craftsmanship is rough, but I made it myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조잡하다'를 관형형으로 써서 만든 솜씨를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing the quality of workmanship.

phrases.en: The stitching on this bag looks sloppy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 거칠게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks rough on the surface.

phrases.en: It's cheap, but it isn't shoddy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 만듦새가 괜찮다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form saying the quality is decent.

explain_en: It describes things, workmanship, writing or design that are not refined and feel rough or cheap. '허술하다' suggests gaps or looseness, while '조잡하다' suggests a rough make or construction. It is used for things people made rather than for personalities.

en: to be major; to be key

examples.en: These two are the most important.
Please summarize only the main points.
I do the less important things later.

examples.ko: 이 부분이 주요해서 꼭 외워야 해요.
examples.en: This part is key, so you must memorize it.
The main reason was the price.
It's a technology that will become more important.

explain: '주요하다' 자체는 글에서 쓰고, 말할 때는 뒤에 명사가 오는 '주요 뉴스', '주요 내용'이 더 흔해요. '중요하다'는 사람이나 일이 소중하다는 느낌, '주요하다'는 여럿 중 중심이 되는 것에 어울려요.

phrases.en: I'll tell you today's main news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '주요하다'보다 명사 앞에 '주요'를 붙이는 모양을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, 주요 before a noun is more common than 주요하다.

phrases.en: The rain is the main reason.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주요한 + 명사'는 글이나 발표에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '주요한 + noun' is used in writing and presentations.

phrases.en: This part isn't that important.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중심이 되는 것이 아니라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is not a central point.

explain_en: The adjective itself is mostly written, and in speech the noun-modifying use, like 'main news' or 'main points', is more common. The word for 'important' suggests something matters to you, while this one fits the central items among many.

examples.en: I can feel sincerity in that person's words.
The truthfulness of this article is doubtful.
A sincere apology is the most important.

examples.ko: 광고에 진실성이 없으면 사람들이 믿지 않아요.
examples.en: If an advertisement has no truthfulness, people don't believe it.
I spoke frankly to show my sincerity.
His sincerity came through in his letter.

explain: 말이나 행동이 거짓 없이 진짜라는 성질을 말해서 '진실성이 있다/없다/느껴지다'로 자주 써요. 사람에게도 쓰지만 기사, 광고, 사과처럼 내용이나 태도에 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: His apology has sincerity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 태도가 진짜라고 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when words or attitude feel genuine.

phrases.en: That ad doesn't seem honest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿기 어렵거나 꾸민 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something feels hard to trust or staged.

phrases.en: I want to receive a sincere apology.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun as a modifier.

explain_en: It names the quality of words or actions being genuine and without lies, used as '진실성이 있다/없다/느껴지다'. It can describe a person, but is used more for content or attitude, such as articles, ads and apologies.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말과 행동이 늘 진중해요.
examples.en: That person is always composed in both words and actions.
He took part in the meeting with a serious, composed attitude.

examples.ko: 나이에 비해 아주 진중하게 생각하는 편이에요.
examples.en: For his age, he tends to think in a very mature, steady way.

examples.ko: 진중하지 못한 말 한마디가 오해를 만들었어요.
examples.en: One careless word created a misunderstanding.

examples.ko: 형은 진중해서 쉽게 화를 내지 않아요.
examples.en: My older brother is steady, so he doesn't get angry easily.

examples.ko: 결정을 내릴 때는 좀 더 진중해야 해요.
examples.en: When making a decision, you need to be more careful and steady.

explain: 말과 행동이 가볍지 않고 무게가 있다는 뜻이라서 사람의 태도나 성격에 주로 써요. '신중하다'는 조심해서 행동한다는 쪽이 강하고, '진중하다'는 점잖고 묵직한 느낌이 있어요. 반대말은 '가볍다'예요.

phrases.en: He is a quiet and prudent person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 사람의 성격을 설명할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe a person's character.

phrases.en: In the meeting, he spoke in a serious, composed manner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍지 않고 점잖은 태도로 말하거나 행동할 때 부사형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form for speaking or acting in a composed, non-casual manner.

phrases.example: 동생은 아직 말과 행동이 진중하지 않아요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is still not prudent in words and actions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍고 경솔한 모습을 부정형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form used to describe light or careless behavior.

explain_en: It describes a person whose words and actions are weighty rather than light, so it is mostly used for attitude or personality. '신중하다' stresses acting carefully, while '진중하다' has a dignified, steady feel. The opposite is '가볍다'.

en: to be true; to be right

examples.ko: 참다운 친구는 어려울 때 곁에 있어 줘요.
examples.en: A true friend stays by your side in hard times.
The teacher's life was truly genuine.

examples.ko: 말보다 행동으로 참답게 사는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: Living truly through actions rather than words is important.

examples.ko: 참답지 않은 칭찬은 오히려 듣기 불편해요.
examples.en: Insincere praise is actually uncomfortable to hear.
You don't have to try hard to look genuine.
To be genuine, your words and actions must match.

explain: '참다운 친구', '참다운 사랑'처럼 이름에 걸맞게 진짜인 모습을 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 '참되다'는 진실하고 올바르다는 느낌이고, 둘 다 글이나 연설에서 자주 만나요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '참다워요', '참다운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 참다운 친구는 힘들 때 알 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can tell a true friend in hard times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름에 걸맞은 진짜 친구를 말할 때 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical pairing for a friend who truly deserves the name.

phrases.en: Let's think about what true love is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 이야기에서 자주 만나는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in writing and speeches.

phrases.en: I want to live truly and honestly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 삶의 태도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes one's attitude toward life.

explain_en: It describes the genuine form of something worthy of its name, as in '참다운 친구' and '참다운 사랑'. The similar '참되다' feels truthful and upright, and both are common in writing and speeches. It is ㅂ-irregular, giving '참다워요' and '참다운'.

examples.en: I'm in top condition today.
This hotel provides the best service.
Top-grade meat is expensive.

examples.ko: 시험 전날에는 푹 자서 컨디션을 최상으로 만드세요.
examples.en: The night before an exam, sleep well and get your condition to its best.
They pick and sell only top-quality rice.

examples.ko: 최상의 결과를 위해 모두 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: Everyone worked hard for the best result.

explain: 최상은 가장 높은 단계라는 뜻으로 '최상의 서비스', '최상 등급'처럼 가격이나 품질을 말할 때 많이 써요. 반대말은 '최하'예요. '최고'는 사람이나 물건 모두에 쓰지만 최상은 상태와 등급에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I hope I'll be in top condition on exam day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '최상의 + 명사' 형태로 상태가 가장 좋을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pattern 최상의 + noun describes the best possible state.

phrases.en: This restaurant uses only top-grade beef.
phrases.nuance_ko: 품질이나 등급이 가장 높다는 뜻으로 물건 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to mean the highest quality or grade.

phrases.en: The weather is the best today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'를 붙여 상태가 가장 좋다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 이다 states that a condition is the very best.

explain_en: 최상 means the highest level, and is common for price and quality, as in '최상의 서비스' and '최상 등급'. The opposite is 최하. 최고 works for people and things, but 최상 fits condition and grade better.
